findings: and it holds its state as the day warms -> and it keeps its condition as the day warms (q3 option C, second clause - new in fleet-repair-2)
justification: Native read-aloud of title, passage, prompts, options and all five rationales, with two sentences read either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. All eight round-2 findings are discharged. Passage: “A maximum-minimum thermometer hung by the gate overnight” replaces the unidiomatic “had gone up” - the repair took an intransitive stative rather than my prescribed passive, and it reads better than what I asked for, with “by the gate” resolving to the locative on the first pass because a gate cannot be an agent of hanging; “Heaters have been costed and not ordered” is the correct bare plural; “more than a month of winter lessons” restores the natural head noun and the ellipsis of takings reads cleanly. Rationales: q1 now teaches “The two figures moved in opposite arithmetic directions, one down and one up, and both of them say the floor was harder in the cold”, which is stronger than the round-2 prescription and is not in conflict with the passage’s “they moved together”, since the passage’s colon expands “together” as in-concert and the rationale supplies the arithmetic; q4’s key paragraph now reads “what he does claim”, which points the right way at last; q4’s B rebuttal quotes the injury-record clause whole and the round-2 dangling pronoun is gone, with “the two” reaching back cleanly to “how the floor rides, not what the floor does to a horse”. The four rebuilt options read as English: “She treats the riders’ account as the thing the readings were brought in to correct” and “She rates the trade’s brochures the fuller answer to the question the yard is asking” both hold (rate + NP + NP is attested BrE, and a plural subject may take a singular predicate nominal); q5 A’s “freezing to one another” is right and its indefinite “a school with no heating” matches the generic register of its siblings. Two rewritten epigrams, “fibre keeps sand from packing” and “The yard wants to know whether any of this keeps a horse sound”, both read as ordinary journalism. The one snag on the read is q3 C: “it holds its state” is a near-miss collocation for a wax coating - English holds a shape, a form, a temper or a condition, and “state” pulls towards state-of-matter, which paraffin does not change here. Checked and cleared: “the pan” in paragraph 5 is unglossed on first mention but is standing agricultural usage in this register and no item turns on it; “though not in the way the yard had blamed it” is compressed but is a recognised elliptical frame.

findings: The other arenas include “some of them older than this one”, and the waxed floors swing whatever age they are. -> The other arenas are a mixed set – “some of them older than this one” – and the waxed floors swing whatever age they are. (q3 rationale, option A rebuttal)
justification: Systematic class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, tested mechanically and not by eye: every span between U+201C and U+201D in all five rationales was extracted with a regex and tested with `span in passage` against the shipped passage string - 31 spans, 31 literal members, 0 near-misses, 0 failures, on fleet-repair-2’s bytes. That includes both spans whose terminal stop moved inside this round (“...lower down it was nearer 3.” and “The tester measures a surface; there is no horse above the cone.”), which grew by the passage’s own full stop and still return True, and the newly whole-quoted “readings from a hundred and forty arenas and injury records he would trust from hardly any of them”. Round-2 vote-2 findings all discharged: the key paragraph of q4 now reads “what he does claim” and no longer teaches against its own key; the q4 B rebuttal no longer strands a pronoun; q1’s key paragraph no longer says both figures moved the same way. Direction audit on every rationale: q1 C down/up and harder-in-cold correct; q1 D correctly inverts the seasons-versus-arenas comparison; q2 A correctly reports the wax as better at the bottom; q2 C correctly reports the unturned layer as firm and under hoofprints; q4 C correctly identifies the riders’ account as borne out and the yard’s three explanations as what is corrected; q5 A correctly separates a stiffened coating at three degrees from ice; q5 D correctly preserves the temperature-over-tractor ranking. Countability, articles, tense/aspect, NPIs (“hardly any”), relatives, mixed comparisons and register: clean. Diagnosis currency: every rebuilt option (q3 C, q4 C, q4 D, q5 A) is diagnosed as it now stands. One structural defect stands, and it is not new - it survived rounds 1 and 2: in the q3 A rebuttal the host frame will not take the quoted fragment. “The other arenas include some of them older than this one” is ill-formed, because “include” cannot take “some of them” with “them” denoting the very set that is the subject; the quotation has to be set off as an appositive rather than governed by the verb.

Variety and typography per layer, swept mechanically over the shipped bytes. Declared BrE, and carried in the student-facing layers, not only the rationale: title (“Reading the Floor”) - no discriminator, which a three-word title cannot be expected to supply; passage - levelling, fibre, millimetres, per cent, boot, livery yards, indoor school, booked in; prompts - none orthographic; options - fibre, millimetres, tines; rationales - fibre, per cent, ageing, artefact. A targeted AmE regex over all five layers (color/fiber/meter/liter/center/-ize/-ization/analyze/leveling/aging/artifact/percent/gotten/toward/gray/spoiled/defense/tire/trunk/railroad/neighbor and the rest) returned zero hits in every layer. Typography per layer: passage U+2019 4, U+2013 4, U+201C/U+201D 2/2; prompts U+2019 1; options U+2019 4; rationales U+2019 6, U+2013 2, U+201C/U+201D 31/31. U+2014 zero everywhere; U+0027 zero everywhere; U+0022 zero everywhere; every curly pair balanced. QUOTE-TERMINAL PUNCTUATION: the two spans I prescribed in round 2 now carry the stop inside, and the rule the unit now applies is the source-governed BrE logical one that elf-b22-003 argued for - inside only where the cited span reproduces a complete passage sentence that the passage itself terminates with a full stop at exactly that point AND the citation is colon-introduced so that it stands as a sentence in its own right. I re-derived that rule mechanically over all 55 spans in the batch and it predicts the placement of every one: 0 mismatches. The unit’s three near-miss cases are all correct under it - q5 D is colon-introduced and a complete utterance but the passage punctuates it with a comma before “Pallenmoor says”, so the stop is outside; q3 B is a complete passage sentence but is subordinated under “while”, so the stop is outside; q1 D truncates before the source’s stop and continues the host sentence with a colon. Copular epigrams in the passage: 5 (“What it is levelling is not soil”; “The wax is a paraffin blend...”; “Here Pallenmoor is careful, and the care is the most useful thing about him”; “there is no horse above the cone”; “That is a good deal less than the trade’s brochures offer, and it is worth more than they are”), down from 7, because fleet-repair-2 rewrote both of its epigram slots into non-copular gnomic sentences. Length tells: no key is the longest option in any set, and q4’s four options are all exactly 15 words.

Native read-aloud of all five layers, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. Both round-2 findings are discharged: the gap-3 rationale now reads “the far end of the process from the stage being described”, which fixes the empty “the one”, and the gap-5 rationale reads “a room clapping out of keenness”, which is the idiomatic preposition. The two new passage sentences both read as native BrE essay prose. “That part repays noticing.” is an ordinary and rather good BrE idiom, and it earns its place after the opening observation instead of restating it. “The tail marks the seam, and every hall has one.” lands the paragraph cleanly; I tested the pronoun and it is fine - “one” takes the nearer antecedent “the seam”, and the alternative reading (“a tail”) is also true, so neither resolution misleads, and “the seam” though definite on first mention is recoverable from the paragraph’s own sequence of applause, tail and chair-scrape. Read aloud, the cloze frames all take their keys without strain: “Equally, the ending is unanimous”; “the room may not join in”; “the coming-down is a negotiation about how long is decent”; “Although what a hall gives an eight-year-old is wholehearted”; “will give one dutifully”. The closing image of the boy in the second row is the best sentence in the batch and is unchanged. Checked and cleared: “it is not permitted to run long” is transatlantic rather than an AmE marker and is current in BrE meeting and broadcast usage; the unit contains no apostrophe at all in any layer, which is unusual over this much prose but produces no unnatural sentence, since every possessive is avoided by a construction that a native would have chosen anyway (“the recorder player got”, “an eight-year-old”).

Systematic class-by-class sweep plus the cloze-specific checks. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 9 curly-quoted spans across the five rationales extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` - 9 of 9 literal members, 0 failures, re-run on fleet-repair-2’s bytes because the repair touched two passage sentences; neither edited sentence overlaps a cited span, and “it is not the same sound the recorder player got” still matches character for character. CLOZE POS-UNIFORMITY, gap by gap: gap 1 four single-word sentence adverbs/connectives, all four grammatical in the slot with a following comma; gap 2 four bare verbs after “may not”, all four forming real phrasal verbs with “in”; gap 3 four singular abstract nouns from one commercial-social stock; gap 4 four adjectives; gap 5 four -ly manner adverbs. In every gap the word class is uniform, every distractor yields a grammatical sentence, and only sense discriminates - which is what the rationales say and what the design requires. SINGLE IDIOMATIC WORD per gap confirmed: no gap admits a second option on an idiomatic reading, and the near-misses are each closed on a stated ground (fall in = form up in ranks; break in / cut in = interrupt; transaction = completed business; bargain = struck outcome taking with/over not about; settlement = closes a dispute; brief agrees with the concession instead of opposing it; rehearsed is denied by the passage; outspoken applies to people and views, not to a noise; narrowly is not a manner adverb for a sound; instinctively is excluded because the room was asked). Calques, countability, articles, tense/aspect, NPIs, relatives, pronoun reach, mixed comparisons and register: clean. Diagnosis currency: each rationale names the options that are in the file now (gap 4 names rehearsed, brief and outspoken; gap 5 names eagerly). No direction is inverted and nothing mis-teaches. Checked closely and cleared: the gap-5 rebuttal of “eagerly” leans on “not the same sound” to exclude a warmer sound, which is a pragmatic rather than a literal entailment, but “it’s not the same” idiomatically means “it is not as good” in exactly this frame, so the teaching holds.

Variety and typography per layer, swept mechanically. Declared BrE. Discriminators per layer: title (“Hands Together”) - none available; passage - realise, organises, plus BrE lexis “school hall”, “a leaving do”, “the second row”; prompts (“Gap (1)”..“Gap (5)”) - none possible; options - none orthographic, which is structural rather than a defect, since all twenty options are single common words and none of them is variety-discriminating (“fall” is the phrasal verb, not the season, so it is not an AmE marker); rationales - organises, unsignalled with the double l, queue, realise. A targeted AmE regex over all five layers returned zero hits. Typography per layer: passage U+2013 1 (the byline dash); prompts none; options none; rationales U+2013 6, U+201C/U+201D 9/9. U+2014 zero, U+0027 zero, U+0022 zero, U+2019 zero in every layer - the unit genuinely contains no apostrophe, and because that is true of the passage and the rationales alike the two layers cannot diverge on apostrophe style. Curly pairs balanced. Quote-terminal punctuation: the unit has one terminal cited span (“it is not the same sound the recorder player got”), it is a mid-sentence fragment of a longer passage sentence, and its stop is outside - which is what the source-governed BrE logical rule requires, and it is consistent with the placement of all 55 spans across the four units (0 mismatches on a mechanical re-derivation of the rule). Copular epigrams in the passage: 6 - “first is the exposed position”, “The risk of putting your hands together in a quiet room is that...”, “Ending is the harder half.”, “the coming-down is a negotiation about how long is decent”, “what a hall gives an eight-year-old is wholehearted”, “the refusal is the message”. That is the highest count of the four units and appropriate to the essay lane; fleet-repair-2 lowered the density rather than raising it, because both sentences it added (“That part repays noticing.”, “The tail marks the seam, and every hall has one.”) are non-copular.

Native read-aloud of all five layers, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. This unit carried no round-2 findings and the repair has not spent its credit. The new closing paragraph, “Nobody has lined the other bins.”, reads better than the beat it replaces: it is an ordinary present perfect with an unforced negative subject, “the other bins” takes its antecedent straight from “Two bins are lined with foam”, and standing alone as a one-sentence paragraph it closes the piece on the size of what is still undone rather than on the remedy - which is the right note for reportage and does not disturb the key. The re-lettering is invisible on the read, because the option texts are untouched. The reordered rationale now runs key, B, C, D, then the mechanism coda, and read aloud in that order it teaches better than the round-2 arrangement, since the coda about which way the potassium travels now falls last where a learner meets it after the options rather than in the middle of them. The passage still reads as a native hospital reportage short throughout: “Carriers drop out of the wall into a bin, one a minute”, “holds a spun tube to the window”, “sent it round the loop for a week”, “a porter walks those down”. Checked and cleared: “what the instrument gave back was that...” is a slightly unusual verb for an instrument returning a result, but it is vivid rather than wrong and it is unchanged from a version that has now passed two rounds.

Systematic class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 7 curly-quoted spans in the single rationale extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` - 7 of 7 literal members, 0 failures, on fleet-repair-2’s bytes. The repair changed a passage sentence and re-lettered the options, so I re-ran rather than assumed: the deleted closing sentence was not quoted anywhere, and the new one is not quoted either, so no span went stale. LETTER-INTEGRITY AFTER RE-LETTERING, the live risk in this unit: every rationale paragraph was matched against the option it names. “Option A is the key” is argued from the accelerometer and the stop at the far end, and A is now “The harm is done at the moment a carrier reaches the far end”; the B paragraph argues from the colour and the ward, and B is the ward-colour option; the C paragraph argues from blood gases, and C is the blood-gases option; the D paragraph argues from the loop speed, and D is the slowed-loop option. The key field is “A”. Not one paragraph refers to a letter it no longer owns, and the paragraphs now run in letter order. Direction audit: the coda states the mechanism the right way round - cells burst first, potassium then passes into the plasma, so the reported figure is too high and not too low, and the pink is haemoglobin released rather than something present beforehand. The B rebuttal correctly denies the ward the colour; the C rebuttal correctly reverses the tube claim; the D rebuttal correctly refuses the slowing. Calques, countability, articles, tense/aspect, NPIs, relatives, pronoun reach, mixed comparisons and register: clean. Diagnosis currency: all four options are diagnosed as they now stand.

Native read-aloud of all five layers, two sentences either side of every fleet-repair-2 span. The round-2 finding is discharged: the B rebuttal now reads “two sentences remove it” and names the second by what it does, “the sentence that dates the thorn”, so a learner is no longer sent to count sentences. The rebuilt option A reads as clean English on one pass - “Ruddiforth’s neighbour answered the claim without bringing the railway company’s plan into the letters” - and the referent “Ruddiforth’s neighbour” is established by “between two Huntingdonshire farms”. The new closing clause of the A rebuttal, “so it was the neighbour’s side that brought the railway into the letters”, is a clean it-cleft and puts the correction where a learner will meet it. The passage is unchanged and still reads as period-accurate English historical essay prose: the hedge-and-ditch arrangement (“cut from above by one and cleaned from below by the other”), “had stood since the enclosure”, “deposited plan”, “chained and pegged”, “laid the thorn together”. Tense handling holds on the read - the archival present of “The letters run to March; both sides agree...” sits beside the narrative past without jarring, because it describes a document that still exists. Checked and cleared: the A rebuttal uses “it” twice in one sentence with different referents (option A, then the tracing), but the second sits inside a relative clause anchored by “there” to “the file” and resolves without a re-read; “in the file” is a fair extension of “the letters”.

Systematic class-by-class sweep. MISQUOTATION, mechanical: all 8 curly-quoted spans in the rationale extracted by regex and tested with `span in passage` - 8 of 8 literal members, 0 failures, re-tested on fleet-repair-2’s bytes after the terminal stop of “An ash grew in the stone gap; a culvert ran under the lane.” moved inside; moving it grew the cited string by the passage’s own full stop, and the span is still a literal member. The two landmark spans the key turns on, “from the stone gap down to the lane” and “along the bank, from the ash to the culvert”, match character for character, as does the bridging sentence. Round-2 vote-2 finding discharged. DIRECTION AND ATTRIBUTION AUDIT, which is where the rebuilt option A put the unit at risk: the passage has the neighbour’s attorney enclosing the tracing, option A denies that the neighbour brought the plan in, and the rationale corrects it in the right direction and names the right side. “A is a true detail with the two sides exchanged” is a compact but accurate gloss - A takes the one thing the file records and attaches it to the wrong side of the correspondence - and the closing clause makes the attribution explicit, so no learner is left to infer it. The C rebuttal keeps the chronology straight (October pegging before the November claim, telling-order against event-order). The B rebuttal’s arithmetic reconciles: 1839 to November 1845 is six years. The D paragraph’s three-landmark argument is sound, and “it makes no claim about compensation, which never fell due” is consistent with “no land was taken”. Calques, countability, articles, tense/aspect, NPIs (“had never been in dispute”), relatives, pronoun reach, mixed comparisons and register: clean. Diagnosis currency: the A paragraph describes the option that is in the file now, not the one it replaced.
